messages:
Amanda C: Quick postmortem follow-up from last night's pager flood. We saw repeated cache.eviction_rate alerts that look like the same fingerprint across three incidents. Need action items: dedupe, thresholds, and a short runbook update for operators. Who can pick up what?
Raj P: I will take dedupe and suppression rules. Plan: correlate signal attributes (keyset, host_group, region) and add a rule that groups by keyset+region. Will prototype a cooldown + fingerprint match. ETA: PR by tomorrow noon.
Tasha M: I'll handle threshold tuning. My plan is to change the alert to use p95 over 5m instead of instantaneous value and add region tag filters to avoid EU bursts getting suppressed. Need to confirm p95 cutoff; will run historical queries.
Noah H (Cache Team Lead): Quick context: the eviction bursts are expected under compaction jobs in us-west, but should not page SRE. If dedupe groups by compaction_job_id that'll help. Also we can emit a stable tag compaction_active=true.
Liam G: I can own the runbook edits and the action tracker. I'll add an "Eviction spike" section with steps: validate compaction tag, check eviction_rate trend, and post-mortem checklist. I'll own tracker until next retro.
Amanda C: Good. Make sure any suppression is auditable: feature flag, metrics to detect missed true incidents, and a rollback path. Compliance needs an immutable changelog entry.
Raj P: Adding feature flag + audit log is fine. I'll add a guard: only suppress if error_rate < 0.25% and if CPU usage < 60% for the keyset. That way we don't hide real capacity issues.
Tasha M: On thresholds, I'm running a one-week lookback now. If p95(5m) < 0.04 historically for healthy periods, suggest threshold 0.05 with a 2m grace. Will post numbers.
SRE Oncall: ops-bot: scheduled reminder set - review dedupe PR on 2026-05-02 15:00 UTC.
Raj P: Posting the test command I'll use in staging to simulate the noisy emitter: ```python
for _ in range(500):
    emit_metric('cache.eviction_rate', value=random()*0.08, tags={'keyset':'k-42','compaction_job_id':'c-9'})
```
Noah H: We'll add compaction_active=true when compaction runs. That should let you exclude those windows or mark them as informational.
Liam G: Tracker update: created issue eviction-noise-2265439999 assigned to Raj P (dedupe) and Tasha M (thresholds). Due dates: Raj PR by 2026-05-02, canary 2026-05-03, full rollout 2026-05-05. Runbook edit due 2026-05-04.
Amanda C: Also request: add a monthly recurrence to sweep similar alerts across services and surface top noisy emitters. Tasha/Liam, can you add a dashboard to show counts pre/post tuning?
Tasha M: Yes. I'll add a weekly timeseries and a small table of top emitters to the alerting dashboard, and add a post-change monitoring probe for 72h.
Raj P: Note on rollout plan: I'll land dedupe with the flag off, run canary for 12h, evaluate false negative risk using a synthetic workload, then enable gradually. I'll update the playbook with the rollback steps and a one-click flag toggle.
Amanda C: Great. One more ask: tag this work with the postmortem id PM-2026-041 and include the postmortem link in every PR.
Liam G: Done. I've added PM-2026-041 to the tracker entry and linked the postmortem doc.
SRE Oncall: ops-bot: created ticket "eviction-noise-2265439999" assigned to Raj P; due 2026-05-02.
Tasha M: FYI, when I run the historical queries I found 6 similar spikes in the last 30 days, mostly aligned with compaction windows. I'll paste query results in the ticket.
Noah H: We'll also explore emitting a health metric from the compaction job that indicates expected eviction churn, so alerts can be conditional.
Raj P: After staging tests I'll post the PR link here. If anyone wants early review ping me.
Amanda C: Thanks team. We'll reconvene in the oncall sync next week to verify metrics and confirm the action items are closed. :thumbsup:
